newsitem.title: LEBANON: Hamas warns PLO against executing two militants.
newsitem.headline: Hamas warns PLO against executing two militants.

text.p: The Moslem militant group Hamas on Tuesday warned the Palestinian Authority against executing two alleged members of the group convicted of killing a PLO policeman and a civilian.
A Palestinian court sentenced to death on Sunday Khalil al-Sakani and Hatem Aby Wadi for killing policeman Akram Ahmed and civilian Abd Alla al-Danaf in separate incidents in 1995.
It sentenced a third alleged Hamas member, Abd al-Latif al-Ashker, to life in jail for his role in the murders.

"We at the Islamic Movement Hamas, while warning the self-rule (Palestinian) Authority against carrying out the death sentence, see in this unjust decision a renewed assault against our strugglers and an overt attempt to hit at the militant groups," Hamas said in a statement issued in Beirut.
The three defendants shot dead the policeman while trying to steal his weapon and killed Danaf because they suspected he was an agent for Israel, Palestinian judicial officials said.
"As we call on Arafat's authority to go back on the unjust decision, we confirm our commitment to pursuing the path of holy struggle, regardless of the sacrifices," the statement added.
Death sentences in Gaza cannot be carried out without the approval of Palestinian President Yasser Arafat.
Arafat has yet to ratify any of the previous five death sentences handed down since most of the area came under self-rule in 1994.
